citations.narrative:
The facility's night houses for free-roaming birds did not adequately restrict a raccoon from entering, which lead to
predation of six animals over a period of about two months.
According to the applicant, on April 3, 2026, a raccoon entered an outdoor night shelter via a small hole in back wall of the
shelter, reportedly only a few inches wide, and predated 4 animals (3 harlequin ducks and 1 adult rooster). The hole was
promptly repaired.
On May 20, 2026, two additional ducks were predated in a different night house by a raccoon due to inadequate security
measures. This smaller night house fits about two adult ducks and has a single door that can slide up or down. The
applicant left the door open and used a wood plank in front of the open door to provide additional ventilation while
restricting the ducks from exiting. However, a raccoon was able to enter in a gap between the plank of wood and the open
door. There was no secondary security measure for this shelter.
Inadequate security of the birds' night housing lead the predation of these 6 animals.
The facility has since taken measures to repair and secure the night houses. Continue to ensure all housing facilities are
kept in good repair and restrict other animals from entering that may negatively affect the welfare of the birds within.
Housing facilities must employ security measures that contain all birds securely. Such measures may include safety
doors, entry/exit doors to the primary enclosure that are double-door, or other equivalent systems designed to prevent
escape of the birds.

The record of animals on hand is incomplete and incorrect.
The following items were incorrect and/or missing from record of animals on hand:
*** The disposition date for 1 pekin duck that was predated is recorded as 4/20/2026. The applicant stated he does not
remember any animal predated on that date; only on 4/3/2026 and 5/20/2026. The representative believes the record of
4/20 was an error and the true disposition date is 5/20.
** The disposition date for 4 predated Harlequin ducks is recorded as "4/3/26 & 5/20/26". It does not specify which of the 4
ducks were deceased on 4/3 and which ducks were deceased on 5/20.
** On 4/3/2026, a rooster was also predated. This animal's disposition and disposition date was not recorded.
** An additional adult rooster passed away from an unrelated cause, reportedly in May 2026. This animal's disposition
was also not recorded.
Inaccurate and incomplete disposition records prevents complete tracing of animals and animal deaths.
Correct by ensuring this facility makes and maintains records which fully and correctly discloses information concerning
animals in his or her possession or under his or her control, or which is transported, sold, euthanized, or otherwise
disposed of by that exhibitor. The records shall include the date of disposal of the animals.

The facility does not have a documented exercise plan.
An exercise plan is necessary to ensure that dogs are provided with appropriate opportunity for exercise for their health
and well-being, with guidance from their attending veterinarian.
The applicant must develop, document, and follow an appropriate plan to provide dogs with the opportunity for exercise.
The plan must be approved by the attending veterinarian.
This is a 1st Re-License Inspection for a Class C license. The inspection and exit briefing were conducted with facility
representatives.
All items must be in compliance within 2 more inspections or by August 11, 2026, or the applicant will forfeit the license
fee and must wait 6 months to reapply. Please contact your inspector to schedule your next Re-License Inspection.
Regulated activity can continue under your existing USDA license until it expires.
